subject.title: feat(agents): per-agent outbound A2A allowlist override

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `agents.list[].tools.agentToAgent.allow` as the per-agent outbound A2A authorization contract now, or should this wait for the broader session-visibility permission model?
rationale: This PR adds a new user-facing config and SDK-visible authorization shape for cross-agent session tools, which is a product/security-boundary choice rather than a purely mechanical bug fix.

options.title: Accept the narrow outbound override after repair
options.body: Normalize exact allow entries, remove the changelog edit, rebase, and land the focused outbound-only contract while broader session visibility remains separate.

options.title: Defer to the broader permission model
options.body: Pause or close this branch and fold per-agent A2A into https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/59149 or https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/48785.

options.title: Redesign the contract shape first
options.body: Ask for an explicit maintainer design on outbound-only versus bidirectional/receivesFrom semantics before accepting any config surface.

recommendation.title: Accept the narrow outbound override after repair
recommendation.body: Normalize exact allow entries, remove the changelog edit, rebase, and land the focused outbound-only contract while broader session visibility remains separate.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest recent history across the SDK/config authorization surface and adjacent A2A matcher hardening commits.
